title: Gravitational Waves
subtitle: A new sense for the Universe
description: Interactive walk through spacetime ripples, LIGO-class interferometers, chirps, GW150914, detector networks, GW170817, and multi-messenger astronomy. Labs are illustrative; event cards cite LIGO/Virgo and observatory sources.
source_note: Wave/interferometer labs ILLUSTRATIVE with exaggerated strain. Chirp tones are ILLUSTRATIVE SONIFICATIONS. Event references: LIGO/Virgo publications and ESO/Hubble host imaging.

steps.title: Ripples in spacetime
steps.narration_text: Gravitational waves are ripples in spacetime itself. They are not sound in air, and they are not a rubber sheet you can grab—they are tiny, traveling changes in distance.

steps.title: What makes a gravitational wave?
steps.narration_text: Accelerating masses with changing quadrupole moments can radiate gravitational waves. Compact binaries—black holes and neutron stars—are the stars of the current detector band.

steps.title: Stretch and squeeze
steps.narration_text: Use the wave lab to compare plus and cross polarizations. Remember: deformations are ILLUSTRATIVE and greatly exaggerated—real strains at Earth are about 10 to the minus 21.

steps.title: How LIGO measures the almost impossible
steps.narration_text: Laser light splits into perpendicular kilometer-scale arms and recombines. A passing wave changes the relative optical path lengths enough—just barely—for a sensitive photodetector to notice.

steps.title: Binary inspiral
steps.narration_text: As a compact binary loses energy to gravitational waves, the orbit tightens and the wave frequency climbs toward merger.

steps.title: Hear the chirp
steps.narration_text: Advance the chirp slider and optionally play the browser tone. That tone is an ILLUSTRATIVE SONIFICATION—frequency-shifted for human ears—not detector-band audio and not sound traveling through space.

steps.title: GW150914
steps.narration_text: GW150914 was the first direct detection: a binary black-hole merger observed by LIGO in September 2015. There is no honest single Stellarium host for its broad localization region.

steps.title: Finding the source
steps.narration_text: Hanford, Livingston, Virgo, and KAGRA form a network. Timing and antenna patterns constrain a sky probability region—often many square degrees—not always a pinpoint.

steps.title: GW170817
steps.narration_text: GW170817 was a binary neutron-star merger with a three-detector gravitational-wave signal and an electromagnetic counterpart in NGC 4993. Stellarium can focus that host galaxy as sky context.

steps.title: Multi-messenger astronomy
steps.narration_text: Waves plus gamma rays, optical/infrared kilonova light, X-rays, and radio together revealed physics neither messenger could give alone—from nuclear matter to cosmic expansion.

steps.title: A new sense for the Universe
steps.narration_text: We now listen to spacetime as well as to light. Exit and Restore returns Stellarium to the capture from when you started.
